- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may lag; add a small upward bias to the early part of the forecast horizon.  
- Mean reversion is evident when model overestimates near 30-day highs; apply a gentle downward taper toward historical mean (last 10–15 days).  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before extrapolation.
